This avoids static bet allocation pitfalls like overexposure early on or underutilization near deadlines. The wealth update rule W_i^m = W_{i-1}^m(1 + l_i(X_i - m)) embodies a multiplicative drift process that reflects the cumulative effect of past outcomes. By incorporating variance estimates through v̂, the system adapts to data variability without requiring explicit variance knowledge. The key insight is that optimal confidence intervals require both tightness and coverage guarantees—STaR-Bets achieves this by ensuring that the final wealth W_n falls into {0, 1/δ}, thereby satisfying the necessary condition for exact coverage. The failure mode occurs when the algorithm fails to converge to one of these states due to numerical instability or incorrect parameterization, leading to invalid confidence intervals.
